data.narrative:
Phaidra is a Series B AI & Software company founded by Jim Gao (ex-Google DeepMind industrial AI lead), Vedavyas Panneershelvam (AlphaGo engineer), and Katherine Hoffman (ex-Trane, Raytheon). The company has raised $120M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of one public company (Palantir) and eight private-stage peers, including Physical Intelligence, Black Forest Labs, and Field AI.

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $120M raised proxy, implying $228M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables (Physical Intelligence at $5.6B, Black Forest Labs at $3.2B, Field AI at $2.0B) yields a median valuation of $3.2B, with a range of $2.0B to $5.6B. The substantial dispersion reflects heterogeneity in model maturity, go-to-market traction, and commercial readiness within the Series B AI cohort.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $194M (floor) to $3.7B (ceiling), with a median of $1.7B. The wide band reflects tension between stage-progression mechanics—which conservatively extrapolate from deployed capital—and peer comparables, which capture the frontier-AI premium. Key uncertainties include Phaidra's revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and proof-of-concept velocity relative to the comp set. Additional operational and market-size diligence is required to narrow this range.
